finding_materiality_spotcheck.evidence: Re-audit (2026-08-20) marked RESOLVED via test_rename_only_diff_is_flagged_by_fence. Confirmed live: the test asserts `res.passed is False and any('supabase/migrations/2026/renamed.sql' in f for f in res.findings)` against a diff with only `rename from`/`rename to` headers (no +++/---). gate_fence.py contains `_RENAME_FROM_RE`/`_RENAME_TO_RE` regexes (L21-22) that parse exactly this diff shape. era_comparison_from_csvs.method: Summed per-cascade columns from out/cascades.csv, grouped by era.

pre_auditor.note: gates_files == 0 across all 35 pre-auditor cascades, not just 'low' -- the GATES.md/gate-waiver mechanism and the post-review-log delta tracking that produces delta_zero_rows literally did not exist as skill features before the auditor phase was added. COVERAGE.md corroborates: pre-auditor findings R/Y/G == 0/0/0 (0 audits ever ran).

era_comparison_from_csvs.conclusion: Not a rate difference -- an existence difference. Gate-waivers and umbrella-delta tracking are post-auditor-era-only instrumentation, so 'meaningfully different' understates it: pre-auditor cascades have literally zero denominator for both metrics. Within the post-auditor era itself, both rates are high: 41.3% of post-review-log rows record a +0 umbrella delta, and gate waivers appear in the large majority of gates files (41 waivers across 52 gates files).

category_skew.method: Findings.csv has no native CATEGORY_VOCAB field; categorized each finding's free-text 'text' column by keyword heuristic against the 9 fixed categories. This is approximate -- many findings.csv rows are truncated table-row fragments (e.g. bare IDs like 'Q3 one row per finge...') that don't contain enough text for confident keyword classification, so a large 'other/unclassifiable' bucket is expected and should not be read as a real 'other' finding-type share.
category_skew.population_note: findings.csv has 354 post-auditor rows and 3 post-admission-audit rows, but ZERO pre-auditor rows (pre-auditor cascades never ran a test-auditor -- COVERAGE.md: pre-auditor R/Y/G == 0/0/0). So 'category skew between eras' cannot be computed pre- vs post-auditor at all: 100% of every category's findings come from the post-auditor (or post-admission-audit) era by construction, not because of any behavioral skew.

category_skew.conclusion: Cannot answer the literal pre-vs-post-auditor category-skew question because pre-auditor has 0 findings. Within post-auditor findings that were classifiable, spec-field-unasserted (13.6%) and tautology (8.5%) are the two most common named categories -- consistent with the zero-test-AC deep-dive above, where most 'zero test' flags similarly trace back to assertion/coverage gaps rather than structural issues like cross-file-conflict or wrong-severity (both rare, 1 and 0 hits respectively).

notes: Headline finding: across all 18 zero-test-flagged ACs in the 5 Agora cascades, ZERO were found to be real-gap (implementation actually violating an untested rule). 13 of 18 are ac_index false-negatives -- the tests exist in the live repo and directly assert the AC, but weren't captured in ac_index['tests'] (likely because the extraction script links tests to ACs only via audit-finding citations, and these ACs were never flagged as a problem by the audit, so no citation existed to extract). 1 of 18 (cascade-qa-profile AC-1) is a genuine, real test gap (no test asserts load_qa_profile's specific ProfileError branches anywhere in the repo) but the shipped implementation is still correct on inspection. The remaining 4 (all cascade-director) are not-applicable because that cascade never got an admitted implementation at all -- confirmed independently by grepping for qa_director.py (does not exist) and the missing heading/kind/extra kwargs on qa_explore.py's user_turn/finish_session.

Implication for COVERAGE.md's headline '147/371 ACs with zero tests' statistic: based on this 18-AC sample, that number is likely substantially overstated as a measure of real coverage gaps -- most zero-test flags in this corpus reflect extraction/attribution methodology (test exists but wasn't linked to its AC), not missing tests. This should be treated as a methodology caveat on the whole ac_coverage.csv zero-test corpus, not just the Agora subset, since the same extraction logic presumably produced it for leandrc49/switchboard/the-best-salesmen too.

Materiality spot-check: 7 of 8 findings checked were material-fix (the audit-flagged gap was real and the applied fix closed it with a genuinely enforcing assertion, verified by reading the live test file). 1 of 8 was already-moot (auditor correctly identified the behavior was already covered elsewhere and left it open, non-blocking, with no fix needed or made). 0 of 8 were cosmetic (i.e., a fix was made but didn't actually change what the test could catch) -- every material-fix case involved either a real bypass (rename-only diff fence evasion), a real tautology risk (self-test stub-passable, raising=False silent no-op), a real measurement-validity gap (scale probe missing generator methods), or a real masking risk in shared test infrastructure (umbrella base_url).

Reverted == 0 and post_review_regressions == 0 across all 56 cascades in every era (cascades.csv). No cascade in this entire corpus ever had a leaf's admitted work reverted or flagged as a post-review regression -- worth noting as either a strong positive signal for the admission gate, or (alternatively) as evidence the corpus is too small/skewed toward successful runs to observe reversion behavior; cannot distinguish between these from the CSVs alone.

gate_waivers (41) and gates_files (52) are both post-auditor-only columns; pre-auditor and (oddly) post-admission-audit cascades show 0 for both, meaning either the mechanism didn't exist yet (pre-auditor, confirmed by 0 audits ever running) or wasn't exercised (post-admission-audit, only 3 cascades, small n).

cascade-driver shard-A never received a re-audit round in the extracted data (reaudit_red=0, reaudit_yellow=0 in audits.csv despite 8 declared yellow findings in pass-1) -- I could not find a re-audit record confirming those 8 yellow findings were independently re-verified as fixed by a second auditor pass. I checked one (Y7, verbatim->substring) directly against the live test file and found it fixed exactly as suggested, but the other 7 (Y1-Y6, Y8) were not part of my 8-item spot-check and their fix status rests only on the fact that the leaf was ultimately admitted (admitted=8 for cascade-driver in cascades.csv), not on independent re-audit verification in this corpus.
